query: was it meant to be permanent?
answer: No, it wasn't meant to be permanent. Gustave Eiffel was granted a 20-year permit, so the tower was supposed to come down in 1909, when the land would go back to the City of Paris [1][2]. It survived because it proved useful for science, especially as a giant radio antenna. Radiotelegraphy experiments started there in 1898 [1]. The tower's ability to send and receive signals was valuable enough that it was allowed to stay after the permit ran out, and it later helped France's military communications in World War I [1][3]. Sources don't agree on exactly how the permit was renewed. Some say it was extended indefinitely and others say it was extended for 70 years, so I haven't picked one.
